_note: Editable, ILLUSTRATIVE rules for Loan Pre-Flight. They are not any lender's policy. Saathi never invents eligibility rules, rates or approval decisions; everything comes from these values and the user's own inputs.

credit_score_bands.note: Often acceptable; offers may be costlier.
Some lenders may decline or charge more.
Many lenders decline unsecured loans in this range.

rejection_reasons.title: Credit score below the lender's requirement
rejection_reasons.explanation: The lender's minimum credit score was not met. Scores fall with late payments, high card usage, defaults and many recent loan enquiries.
actions: Pay every EMI and card bill on time for the next 6-12 months.
Bring card usage below 30% of your limit.
Check your credit report for errors and dispute them with the bureau.

rejection_reasons.title: Too much of your income already goes to EMIs
rejection_reasons.explanation: Lenders check what share of your income is already committed to EMIs and card dues. A new EMI would push it above their limit.
actions: Close or prepay a small existing loan first.
Ask for a smaller amount or a longer tenure.
Add a co-applicant with income.

rejection_reasons.title: Overdue, settled or written-off accounts on your report
rejection_reasons.explanation: Missed payments (DPD), settlements or write-offs signal repayment risk and are a common reason for rejection.
actions: Clear any overdue amount immediately.
For settled accounts, ask the lender about paying the balance and getting a 'closed' status.
Get a no-dues certificate and check your report is updated.

rejection_reasons.title: Too many recent loan or card applications
rejection_reasons.explanation: Several applications in a short time make you look credit-hungry and each one can lower your score slightly.
actions: Avoid new applications for 3-6 months.
Use soft-check eligibility tools instead of formal applications.
Apply to one lender at a time.

rejection_reasons.title: High credit card usage
rejection_reasons.explanation: Using a large share of your card limit suggests financial stress.
actions: Pay down card balances below 30% of the limit.
Pay before the statement date so a lower balance is reported.

rejection_reasons.title: Not enough credit history
rejection_reasons.explanation: The lender could not assess you because your credit history is short or empty.
actions: Start with a small secured credit card or a credit-builder loan.
Use it lightly and pay in full every month.

rejection_reasons.title: Income or employment could not be verified or is too new
rejection_reasons.explanation: Lenders need stable, provable income and often a minimum time with your employer or in business.
actions: Submit complete income proof (salary slips, ITR, bank statements).
Reapply after completing the lender's minimum job or business tenure.

rejection_reasons.title: Documents incomplete or details not matching
rejection_reasons.explanation: Missing documents or mismatched details (name, date of birth, address) stop the application.
actions: Make sure your name and date of birth match across PAN, Aadhaar and bank records.
Submit every document on the checklist.

rejection_reasons.title: Age or location outside the lender's policy
rejection_reasons.explanation: Lenders lend only within certain age ranges and serviceable areas.
actions: Ask which lenders serve your location and age group.
Consider a co-applicant within the lender's criteria.

explanations.prepayment: Prepayment means paying part of the loan early. It reduces the interest you pay and can shorten the tenure. RBI does not allow prepayment charges on floating-rate loans taken by individuals for non-business purposes; fixed-rate and business loans may have charges, so check your agreement.
explanations.foreclosure: Foreclosure means closing the whole loan before its tenure ends. You pay the outstanding principal (plus any charges allowed by your agreement) and save the remaining interest. Ask for a no-dues certificate and check your credit report shows the loan as closed.
explanations.interest: Your EMI is mostly interest in the early years and mostly principal later. A higher rate or a longer tenure increases the total interest you pay, even if the EMI looks smaller.
explanations.late_payment: A late EMI usually brings a penalty charge and is reported to credit bureaus. Even one payment 30+ days late can lower your credit score and make future loans harder or costlier. Repeated non-payment can lead to recovery action.

disclaimer: This is not a loan approval, credit decision, or guarantee of eligibility. Rules and thresholds used here are illustrative; the lender decides.
